newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Aetna restructures, takes charge.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Aetna restructures, takes charge.

text.p: Aetna Inc said Thursday it would restructure its health care business and retirement services, resulting in the elimination of more than 4,000 health care unit jobs and charges in the third and fourth quarters. A full text of the company's statement follows.
Aetna to restructure businesses; Record 1996 third and fourth quarter charges
Business Editors
HARTFORD, Conn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 10, 1996--
-- $32 Million After-Tax Charge in Third Quarter Related to Retirement Services --
-- $275 Million After-Tax Charge in Fourth Quarter Related to Health Integration --

Aetna (NYSE: AET) today announced that it will record after-tax restructuring charges against third and fourth quarter 1996 operating earnings. An after-tax charge of approximately $32 million (or $0.22 per share) will be recorded in the third quarter of 1996 related to restructuring actions in its retirement services business. An after-tax charge of approximately $275 million (or $1.82 per share) related to the integration of its health business following the merger with U.S. Healthcare will be recorded in the fourth quarter of 1996.

"With these actions, we are creating the right organizational structure to provide high quality health care coverage and retirement services at affordable prices," said Aetna Chairman Ronald E. Compton. "Through focused, cost efficient operations and smart use of advanced technology, we will be better able to realize our growth potential.

"Although we will always make it a priority to maintain a competitive cost structure, we will now focus on growing our businesses. Over the long term, we believe this growth will result in more job opportunities," Compton said.
Aetna Retirement Services

The third quarter 1996 charge in Aetna Retirement Services (ARS) principally relates to severance and other costs associated with expense reduction and process redesign efforts of customer service and other business support functions. Approximately 400 net positions will be reduced nationally in ARS. The net reduction takes into account the addition of new jobs as well as attrition and job eliminations. The cost of approximately 700 job eliminations, to be completed in the first quarter of 1998, has been provided for in the third quarter charge.

"Aetna Retirement Services was formed this year through the combination of several separate business units, to enable us to present one face to customers and to fulfill their demand for top-quality, affordable retirement products and services," said Daniel P. Kearney, executive vice president and head of Aetna Retirement Services. "The efficiencies we will gain from consolidation and process redesign, as well as the use of new technology, will allow us to provide our products and services at a price and value appropriate for the highly competitive financial services market."
Aetna U.S. Healthcare

The fourth quarter 1996 after-tax restructuring charge is principally related to costs associated with the integration of the Aetna and U.S. Healthcare health businesses, now named Aetna U.S. Healthcare. Of the total after-tax charge, $167 million is for severance costs, $40 million is facilities-related and $68 million is for asset write-offs and other related items. As part of the merger integration process, Aetna U.S. Healthcare is implementing a regional structure for all sales, network management, underwriting, provider contracting, physician relations and customer service centers.

"Our regionalized structure will enhance our position as the leading managed care company with a commitment to quality," said Joseph T. Sebastianelli, co-president of Aetna U.S. Healthcare. "This regional approach will position us as the first truly national managed care organization with the broad reach, capabilities and operating flexibility to provide our members, employer groups and network providers with the products and services they demand. Importantly, our new structure will further our commitment to quality, which includes our strategic partnerships with prominent academic medical centers across the country."

"As part of our commitment to provide health care coverage to Americans in all parts of the nation, we will maintain a sizable presence in every broad geographic region of the country," said Michael J. Cardillo, co-president of Aetna U.S. Healthcare. The six regional headquarters are:
-- Middletown, CT (Northeast Region)
-- Blue Bell, PA (Mid-Atlantic Region)
-- Atlanta, GA (Southeast Region)
-- Chicago, IL (Midwest Region)
-- Dallas, TX (West Central Region)
-- Walnut Creek, CA (West Region)
To align the organization with this regional structure, Aetna U.S. Healthcare will:

-- Accelerate consolidation of over 40 customer service centers into larger and more efficient centers with the use of advanced technology. The merger accelerates the timetable for Aetna's plans to consolidate its health service centers and move from a paper-based to an electronic claims processing system. In 1998, Aetna U.S. Healthcare expects to have six regional service centers, supported by secondary sites serving specific customer and geographic needs (see attached Fact Sheet); and

-- Reconfigure medical delivery functions regionally to further strengthen patient and provider relationships. Regional medical delivery centers will be responsible for all clinical management, including disease and patient management, clinical guidelines, credentialing and accreditation. These centers will be located close to major medical institutions in order to benefit from closer ties to these institutions as well as the availability of highly skilled medical professionals.

"The regional alignment of medical delivery will allow us to place an intense emphasis on the quality of care our members receive and to work closely with our providers to develop an environment where continuous quality improvement occurs," Sebastianelli said.
As part of the merger integration process, Aetna U.S. Healthcare will also:
-- Rationalize duplicate core administrative functions to eliminate overlap; and
-- Shift to a single managed care technology platform based on the U.S. Healthcare model, and reduce the number of data centers from three to two.
"As we combine operations, we are establishing the cost structure, regional organization and systems and infrastructure needed to realize our full growth potential," Cardillo said.

The actions announced today are in line with the previously-announced target of $140 million of after-tax administrative expense synergies, and puts Aetna U.S. Healthcare well on the way to achieving the previously announced target of $300 million of total after-tax synergies within 18 months from closing of the merger.

These initiatives are expected to result in a net workforce reduction in Aetna U.S. Healthcare of approximately 4,000. The cost of approximately 7,500 job eliminations, to be completed by the end of 1998, has been provided for in the fourth quarter charge. However, job growth is expected in some areas such as sales and marketing, and the regional consolidation of service centers and other functions will require a workforce reduction in some locations and the addition of jobs in others. As a result, the net reduction takes into account the addition of new jobs as well as job eliminations and normal attrition.

"As these restructurings proceed, we will also be sensitive to the needs of our employees, fulfilling our promise to rely as much as practicable on attrition," Compton said. "We will seek to give qualified employees opportunities for new jobs and reasonable levels of retraining to prepare them for those opportunities."

Aetna Inc. will report third quarter 1996 results on October 25, 1996 and fourth quarter and year-end 1996 results in February, 1997. The statements contained in this release that are not historical facts are forward looking statements that are based on management's estimates, assumptions and projections. Important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those estimated by management include, among other things, an unexpected increase in competition, an unfavorable pricing environment, the timing and success of integrating Aetna's health business with U.S. Healthcare's, including the ability to achieve expected efficiencies in operations and reductions in medical costs, as well as growth in business. Additional information about these and other factors that could potentially affect the Company's financial results may be found in documents filed by the Company with the Securities and Exchange Commission. -0- Fact Sheet for Aetna U.S. Healthcare restructuring Oct. 10, 1996 Following the restructuring announced today, Aetna U.S. Healthcare will have six regional headquarters around the country. These locations were selected to provide regional representation and because of their proximity to customers, availability of facilities and skilled workforces.
